mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over the previous quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% over the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which boosts related industries and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS decreases by more than 1% in a month.
